items.quote: paths = [Path(arg) for arg in sys.argv[1:]] or runtime_files(Path.cwd().resolve())
items.what: Three copies of the Lua lint command-line driver: tools/lint_taint.py:151-164, tools/lint_multivalue.py:326-341 and tools/lint_copy.py:143-150. Each takes optional file arguments, defaults to runtime_files(root), reads and tokenizes each file, prints path:line hits and returns 1 on any hit. Canonical home: lint_multivalue.py (argparse, root from __file__), which already owns the shared tokenizer.
items.why: Drift between the copies, none with a stated reason: lint_taint reads sys.argv and takes the root from Path.cwd(), the other two use argparse and Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent, so lint_taint only works from the repository root; lint_taint prints read and syntax errors to stderr, lint_multivalue to stdout, and lint_copy catches neither (a LuaSyntaxError or missing file is a traceback); lint_taint imports tools.lint_multivalue and is run as python3 -m tools.lint_taint (tools/typecheck.sh:25) while lint_copy imports lint_multivalue and is run as a script (typecheck.sh:27-28), which is why lint_multivalue.py:9-12 carries an `if __package__` double import and why unittest discovery loads the tokenizer module twice under two names (two LuaSyntaxError classes). A change to how the default file set, the root or a read error is handled has to be made three times.
items.reason: Unify the Lua lint command-line drivers (tools/lint_taint.py:151-164, tools/lint_multivalue.py:326-341, part of tools/lint_copy.py:143-150)? They differ in root (lint_taint uses the working directory, so run outside the repository root it finds no TOC, checks nothing and exits 0), error stream and import style, so one driver changes those.

items.what: screenshots.map_position (tools/screenshots.py:1014-1020) re-derives the world (north, west) -> uiMap (x, y) projection that gen_quests.project (tools/gen_quests.py:231-244) owns, with the same UiMapAssignment Region_1/Region_4, Region_0/Region_3 and UiMin/UiMax arithmetic. items.why: Same formula, same DB2 columns, both read wago.tools rows as string dicts. Differences: project bounds-checks (point inside the Region box, a non-degenerate region, result in 0..1) and returns None otherwise; map_position extrapolates without checks. That difference would need checking for walk points just outside the zone rect (Path.FindSync may step off the uiMap rect), so a switch must handle None. world_point (1003-1011) is the inverse and has no counterpart in gen_quests. The docstring says the math inverts 'SPF's projection', a third copy in another repo.
items.reason: The contracts differ: map_position selects a row for a 2-D point and extrapolates, raising on degenerate spans, whereas project accepts a supplied row and altitude and returns None for out-of-region, degenerate or off-map points. Pinned SPF 061f0b1 Route.lua:88-118 preserves off-map endpoints for segment clipping, AGF map_frame clips after drawing, and a cached Barrens-row probe produced (-0.1, 0.5) versus None, establishing a rendering constraint that requires this divergence.

items.why: The only call is `(walk,) = spf_walks(ui, [(map_id, ...)])`; git grep over every local and remote branch finds no call with a second leg. The plural shape costs an entries list, a `LEGS` table and an ipairs loop with a `walks` accumulator in SPF_PROGRAM, and a wrap and unwrap at the call. Collapsed form: `spf_walk(ui, map_id, start, goal)` that formats one leg, has the Lua program call Path.FindSync once and print one point list, and returns that list.

items.quote: # name: (draw(canvas, entry, rect, layer), its <Size> by (ui, entry) or None, its own <Anchors> or None, frameLevel)
items.what: A stock recipe is a bare 4-tuple whose meaning lives only in this comment, and its one caller module unpacks it by index in four places: tools/screenshots.py:133-134 (`recipe[1]` as the size function), :139-141 (`recipe[2]`, turning (point, x, y) triples into anchor dicts against the parent), :190-192 (`recipe[3]` as a raised-frame flag) and :215-219 (`recipe[0]`, with `if recipe[0] is draw_scroll_frame` to pass that one recipe a fifth argument). tools/screenshots_test.py:103 unpacks it a fifth way (`(draw, *_)`).
items.why: The callers carry what the recipe should own: which slot is which, how a recipe's anchors become resolver anchors, what a non-zero frameLevel means, and which recipe has a different draw signature. Adding a field or a second recipe needing the child height means editing every index site and the identity check in screenshots.py, a file with 23 commits in the last three months. Named fields and a uniform draw call would sit behind the interface; where the seam goes is a design choice.
items.reason: The cited sites are real, but the lens asks for complexity that reappears in each caller, and here there is one caller module (tools/screenshots.py) that reads each slot at exactly one site: size in intrinsic(), anchors in defaults(), frameLevel and draw in Layout.frame(), with the test only taking slot 0. Nothing is repeated, so moving it behind the recipe relocates the four reads rather than removing any, and the claim that a new field means editing every index site is wrong since indices 0 to 3 and `(draw, *_)` survive an appended field; the `recipe[0] is draw_scroll_frame` special case is a single-site wart, not caller-repeated work.

items.what: AGFProviders.GoToEntrance annotates a function that no longer exists: fully dead
items.why: Integrations/Providers.lua defines DungeonEntrance but no GoToEntrance, and the name appears nowhere else in Core, Planning, Integrations, UI, Locales, tests, tools, docs, the TOC or XML; git log -S shows the implementation was removed from the runtime code in commit e268c35 and the annotation stayed (the Stale leftovers anti-pattern). Hard stops do not apply: types/ never loads in game, the name is not built from strings (no Providers[key] dispatch), it is not persisted, and ns.Providers is not part of the public AdventureGuideForever.API (Core/API.lua exposes version, CurrentStop, NextStops only). Checked: dynamic dispatch (no indexed access into Providers), public surface (docs/api.md, Core/API.lua), manifests (TOC, Bindings.xml, Panel.xml), data lookup (Locales, docs), cross-boundary (tools/), open work (only older local branches that predate the removal still carry the old Providers.lua implementation; main does not).
